notes: Eclipse Loop 2.5.1 The mixer, measured against a standard desk. Eight things a mixing engineer reaches for that were not there - and a third of every channel strip that was simply empty. The strip carried a fixed 300px fader centred in whatever space was left, which opened a gap under I/O and another above the pan knob — about a third of every strip was empty while the fader sat squeezed in the middle. The fader now takes that space and sits on a common baseline, so there is real throw where you mix. Solo mode ▸ Pre-fader listen (PFL). A soloed channel is heard at its source level with the fader bypassed, so a channel parked near silence can still be checked. Input trim applies; the VCA group does not. Solo in place remains the default and is unchanged. Solo-safe on a mixer strip, not just an arranger row — it existed on one of the two fader sets, so whether it worked depended on which you were looking at. Meter pre-fader, to read what arrives at the channel rather than what leaves. The clip light latches. It was true for a single frame, which is exactly the overshoot you miss. Click a meter to clear it
